title: Thread a spring-preloaded anti-backlash nut onto a lead screw, its halves pressed together so it keeps full preload
instruction: Thread the anti-backlash nut onto the lead screw with its rear nut pressed home against the spring, so it keeps full preload, and turn it down until the red mark is hidden. Then let go.
context: Robot building: lead-screw axes with spring-preloaded anti-backlash nuts drive linear joints and Z stages of robots, lab-automation gantries and the 3D printers that make robot parts (StepperOnline's TR8x8 lead-screw stepper 17LS19-1684E-200G-AR4 is the J5 motor of the AR4-MK2 robot arm kit). Fitting the nut sets its preload. Makers say to fit its parts together, aligned, with the spring between them (ReliaBot T8 nut), and that the spacing of the two nuts sets the preload, 4 to 8 N (Zyltech ABN-Tr8x8). Kept pressed together while threaded on, the rear nut catches the thread nested, with full preload; let go too early and the screw's end lifts it one or two thread starts out, with half or no preload, and the axis has play. The hard part: pressing the small rear nut home against its 8 N spring while turning the nut and following its 8 mm-per-turn lead, until the screw has passed into the rear nut.
setup: Units mm. Robot base frame: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robots' left from the midpoint between them; heights above the table top. Both arms start at their ready pose. One object, fixed to the table: a lead-screw actuator with its screw vertical at (250, -120). It is a NEMA-17 stepper with an integrated TR8x8 lead screw (VXB 'Nema 17 Stepper Motor With TR8x8 100mm Lead Screw': motor 42.3 x 42.3 x 38.7, black with aluminium end caps, 0.44 N m holding torque; steel screw 8 across, 4 starts 2 apart, 8 mm per turn, 100 out of the motor face). The motor hangs face up under a 60 x 60 x 3 aluminium plate (23 centre hole, four M3 screws on the motor's 31 square) on four M3 x 40 aluminium standoffs 25 from the axis each way, taped to the table with double-sided tape: plate top 43, screw top 140. The motor is powered and holding (any stepper driver, enabled). A red band 1.5 wide is painted round the screw centred 106 above the table (34 below its top). On the screw's top end sits a brass anti-backlash nut for TR8x8 (Zyltech ABN-Tr8x8, 44 g), flange down, dropped onto the thread start but not turned on: the front nut (22 flange 3.5 thick with four 3.5 holes on a 16 circle, 10.2 body, 15 long), a 12 stainless compression spring round its body, and the 14 rear nut (9 long) on top, kept from turning by two guide pins into the flange. Spring free: 5 between the front nut's body and the rear nut, 29 overall; the flange's underside 138 above the table, the rear nut's top 167. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Scored at the end of the trial (the run limit, or once 1.0 has held 1 s). Travel: how far the flange's underside has gone down from its start (138 above the table). Nut length: flange underside to the rear nut's top (29 with the spring free, 25 pressed home). Through: the screw's end level with or above the rear nut's top (0.1 tolerance), so both nuts are on the thread. 1.0: through, nut length 25.5 or less (rear nut nested: 8 N of preload, no axial play), the flange's underside at or below the red band's lower edge (32.75 or more of travel, the whole band hidden), and both grippers 30 mm or more from the nut and the screw's top. 0.75: through and 25.5 or less, but less travel than that or a gripper still near the nut. 0.5: through but longer than 25.5 (the rear nut caught one or two thread starts out, 27 or 29: 4 N or no preload). 0.25: not through, but the nut turned 8 or more down (one turn). 0 otherwise; doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: calipers for the nut length, a steel rule from the plate to the flange's underside for travel, a look at the screw's end and the red band, and the trial video for the grippers' 30 mm.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed; about 1 minute. Turn the nut anticlockwise (seen from above) up and off the screw; the spring pushes the rear nut back out (29 overall). Set it flange down on the screw's end and turn it slowly anticlockwise until it drops onto the thread start; leave it there, not turned on. Once per nut, check that the bare front nut stays where it is left on the vertical screw, and measure its nested length (threaded on by hand, pressed together); score against that length plus 0.5 if it is not 25.
fidelity: PhysX, 240 Hz. Screw and nuts are real-size colliders; the thread is kinematic (front nut 8 mm per turn; drag 0.06 N m to start, 0.06-0.08 turning, not growing with the press). The rear nut slides on the front nut on a 2,000 N/m spring (8 N pressed home, nominal). Thread catch is a rule: when the screw's end reaches the rear nut it takes the first thread start (2 mm apart) at or beyond the screw's end, and keeps that spacing until unthreaded. The motor's holding torque is a fixed screw.
